newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ADAMS AND MURRAY REVITALISE WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ADAMS AND MURRAY REVITALISE WEST INDIES.

text.p: Makeshift spinner Jimmy Adams took five wickets in a career-best haul as West Indies ended a run of seven defeats with an emphatic seven-wicket limited overs win against Pakistan on Tuesday.

Wicketkeeper and part-time opener Junior Murray ensured Adams' efforts were not wasted by smashing a rapid 86 to steer his resurgent side to victory with almost 14 overs to spare in the World Series match at Adelaide Oval.
After restricting Pakistan to 176 all out in 48.4 overs, West Indies reached 177 for three in 36.1 overs after Murray equalled his best score in one-day cricket.
West Indies, who lost their opening two World Series fixtures and the first two test matches against Australia, responded positively to a warning from tour manager Clive Lloyd.
Lloyd, exasperated by West Indies' poor form in Australia, threatened to introduce some fresh faces unless the current slide was reversed and was rewarded with a committed and inventive display.
Murray, promoted to opener to invigorate the top order, hit 14 fours in 79 deliveries during an aggressive innings that lasted two minutes short of two hours.

Adams, a left-arm orthodox spinner and middle order batsman, proved an unlikely inspiration with the ball, claiming the key wickets of Inzamam-ul-Haq and Pakistan captain Wasim Akram among his victims in a 10-over spell that cost 37 runs.

West Indies captain Courtney Walsh abandoned his previous reliance on an undiluted pace attack by using two other makeshift spinners -- Carl Hooper and Shivnarine Chanderpaul -- to good effect on a slow wicket that offered turn.
Veteran fast bowler Curtly Ambrose offered valuable support for the spinners by taking two for 16 in 9.4 overs.
Opener Zahoor Elahi provided the only prolonged resistance with a patient 51 before being run out after a smart piece of fielding by Brian Lara, who scored an unbeaten 31 in West Indies' reply.
Australia lead the triangular competition with four points from three matches, two points clear of both West Indies and Pakistan, who have a game in hand.
